thread:
Sofia Ivanova: ok need to settle on initial short/long split for the prototype. please don’t bikeshed forever but we need something defensible for benchmarks + canary.

Sofia Ivanova: two open questions:
1) threshold: prompt_tokens? predicted prefill cost? wall time?
2) streaming vs non-streaming: do we treat streaming chat as always “short/latency” or just based on prompt?

Lena Fischer: IMO token threshold is simplest but we’ll get burned by model-dependent prefill perf + kv cache hits. A 2k prompt on 7B != 2k prompt on 70B.

Marcus Reed: current prototype classifier only has prompt_tokens at enqueue time. we *can* add a stub for predicted prefill cost but it’ll be a guess until we have runtime feedback.

Omar El-Sayed: from perf side: if we pick token threshold, at least make it per-model-configurable so we can tune in canary w/out code changes.

Julian Moore: also note: prompt_tokens for “streaming” requests isn’t the whole story. Streaming has user-visible latency = TTFT more than total completion. We should bias streaming to the low-latency queue even if prompt is moderate.

Samir Qureshi: careful: if we auto-prioritize all streaming, a single customer can flip streaming=true and starve batch summarization. need some guardrail.

Jonas Weber: +1 on guardrails. perf canary will include a “streaming 70% + long summarization 30%” mix. If we treat all streaming as high-prio, it will look great for p95 on streaming but might destroy throughput.

Rina Kobayashi: what are we targeting as “short”? interactive chat + tool calls: usually prompt 200-800 tokens. long: 4k-32k summarization / RAG w big context.

Lena Fischer: proposal: 2D rule:
- base class by predicted prefill cost
- then “latency_sensitive” hint if streaming OR customer tier OR route tag, but cap share.

Marcus Reed: implementing a cap is more scheduler than classifier. but yes we can do: streaming->short_queue flag, but short_queue has max burst tokens window.

Sofia Ivanova: let’s ground this with data. Omar/Rina do we have any quick microbench numbers from last week?

Rina Kobayashi: yup, from local bench on A100-80GB, llama-3.1-70b-instruct, batch=1-ish (continuous batching on).
Baseline FIFO, mixed arrival (50% prompt=256, 50% prompt=8192), output=128 tokens.

Rina Kobayashi: snippet:
```
scenario: mix_50_50 (256/8192)
mode: non_streaming
baseline_fifo:
  ttft_p50=0.42s ttft_p95=3.88s ttft_p99=6.71s
  e2e_p50=1.31s  e2e_p95=9.02s  e2e_p99=15.4s
  tok/s_gpu=142
2q_shortfirst(th=2048):
  ttft_p50=0.39s ttft_p95=1.26s ttft_p99=2.41s
  e2e_p50=1.29s  e2e_p95=7.96s  e2e_p99=13.8s
  tok/s_gpu=136
```

Jonas Weber: that’s a big win on TTFT p95. tok/s dip 4% which is probably acceptable if stable.

Grace Kim: note: that tok/s drop might also be kernel choice differences if batching shape changed. we should confirm kernel stats same (attention kernel, paging, etc).

Hiro Tanaka: ^ +1. scheduling can change sequence length mix per batch and trigger different kernel paths. at least log selected kernel + effective batch shapes in the bench output.

Omar El-Sayed: we can add a counter for “prefill_batch_tokens” and “decode_batch_tokens” and sample kernel id. but for now, Rina’s bench was pinned to same config; kernel variance small but not zero.

Julian Moore: about threshold: the th=2048 seems ok for that distribution, but for 4k contexts it might classify too much as long, and then short queue becomes tiny.

Lena Fischer: 2048 is arbitrary. maybe use *predicted prefill ms* instead of tokens. threshold like 250ms prefill.

Marcus Reed: we don’t have predicted ms unless we model it. we could approximate prefill_cost = prompt_tokens * k(model, quant, gpu). k can be a constant measured during warmup.

Samir Qureshi: warmup-based k is fragile under contention and kv cache hits.

Omar El-Sayed: alternative: EWMA on observed prefill time per request class and update threshold online (but then classifier uses past data; could oscillate).

Sofia Ivanova: for prototype (week 3-5) we need conservative default w minimal complexity. we can iterate to EWMA later behind same interface.

Jonas Weber: can we just start with token threshold + “streaming bias” but not absolute? like streaming requests get *weight boost* rather than always in short queue.

Julian Moore: I like that: keep two queues but allow “streaming” to reduce effective cost. eg treat streaming prompt_tokens as prompt_tokens * 0.5 for classification.

Lena Fischer: hmm feels hacky but might work. Another option: keep classification by prompt_tokens only, but scheduler uses different service ratio when short queue has streaming backlog.

Marcus Reed: scheduler can do: serve N shorts then 1 long (fairness window). If shorts are streaming, N increases up to cap. This avoids “streaming=true => infinite priority”.

Samir Qureshi: cap needs to be explicit. otherwise under overload you’ll still starve long. what’s the starvation bound we want? 2s? 5s?

Sofia Ivanova: bound in terms of wait time for long queue. e.g. guarantee at least 1 long dispatch every W ms or after K short dispatches.

Rina Kobayashi: streaming vs non-streaming nuance: for streaming, TTFT p95 is the thing. for non-streaming, e2e p95 matters more. If we prioritize streaming too much, non-streaming might regress even if total tok/s is ok.

Omar El-Sayed: we should instrument both. Specifically: (a) queue_wait_ms, (b) prefill_ms, (c) first_token_ms, (d) decode_ms. and break out by stream=true/false.

Grace Kim: also treat “streaming but huge prompt” carefully: a 16k streaming request still has huge prefill and will block shared prefill kernels. can we force those into long queue regardless of streaming?

Lena Fischer: yes: streaming should not override long classification when prompt_tokens is above “definitely long” threshold. like two thresholds: short<=2k, long>=8k, middle uses streaming hint.

Marcus Reed: implementable. 3-bucket:
- <=2k => short queue
- >=8k => long queue
- (2k,8k) => short if streaming else long

Julian Moore: that seems sane. we can tune 2k/8k per model later.

Jonas Weber: do we have numbers with streaming mix? even quick synthetic.

Rina Kobayashi: quick hack run from yesterday (same model/hw), streaming requests use output=256 tokens but we measure TTFT. 70% streaming prompt=512, 30% non-streaming prompt=8192. 

Rina Kobayashi: 
```
scenario: stream70_short512 + batch30_long8192
baseline_fifo:
  stream_ttft_p95=2.94s
  long_e2e_p95=13.1s
2q_shortfirst(th=2048, stream=>short):
  stream_ttft_p95=0.98s
  long_e2e_p95=15.9s
```

Samir Qureshi: long e2e p95 +21% is probably too much for dedicated customers running summarization.

Omar El-Sayed: agreed. That’s the “streaming dominates” effect.

Lena Fischer: if we do the fairness window (e.g. 8 shorts then 1 long), long should come back down.

Marcus Reed: I can add a simple “service quantum”: after serving `short_burst_max=8` dispatches, force a long if any queued. Also enforce `long_max_wait_ms` by checking oldest long enqueue time.

Hiro Tanaka: make sure forced long dispatch doesn’t cause prefill batch to balloon and block. maybe “force long” means allow one long prefill to start, but don’t merge it into a giant prefill batch with other longs if shorts are waiting.

Grace Kim: +1. otherwise we just move the pain around. maybe cap prefill batch tokens per class.

Julian Moore: re streaming: for streaming requests, we can consider prioritizing *prefill* but not necessarily decode? once first token is out, decode latency is less visible (though still matters). But scheduler is mostly at request level, not phase.

Omar El-Sayed: we *can* split scheduling by phase: treat prefill tasks as their own queue units. but that’s bigger change.

Sofia Ivanova: keep it request-level for prototype. phase-aware can be follow-up.

Jonas Weber: action: pick initial thresholds + fairness window defaults for the design doc.

Sofia Ivanova: proposal for v0 (flagged):
- base on prompt_tokens
- short_threshold=2048
- long_threshold=8192
- middle band: streaming=>short else long
- scheduler: two queues, short-first with fairness: max 8 short dispatches in a row; and long_max_wait_ms=2000ms (if exceeded, force long next)
- also cap “short queue share” under overload via admission control later
Thoughts?

Samir Qureshi: 2s max wait for long seems too low? forcing long too often might erase gains. maybe 5s.

Lena Fischer: i’d do 5s for long_max_wait initially. The 8-short burst already gives some bound.

Rina Kobayashi: from the bench, even a tiny amount of long servicing helps long p95 a lot. maybe start with 8:1 and 5s bound, then tune.

Julian Moore: ok but please don’t let streaming mid-band sneak in huge prompts. long_threshold should be hard override.

Grace Kim: ok with 2k/8k as starting points. But add note: per-model config + we’ll validate kernel selection stability in perf suite.

Hiro Tanaka: and log batch composition by class in benchmarks. otherwise we can’t explain regressions.

Omar El-Sayed: i’ll add a debug metric sample for (class, prompt_tokens_bucket, stream) and also “dispatch_reason” (normal_short, fairness_long, max_wait_long).

Marcus Reed: i can implement this classifier quickly. will add config fields: short_threshold_tokens, long_threshold_tokens, short_burst_max, long_max_wait_ms.

Jonas Weber: perf gating: we’ll need one scenario where streaming mix exists, and ensure long p95 doesn’t regress more than X%. We’ll align on X in perf standard update.

Sofia Ivanova: ok locking v0 as above with long_max_wait_ms=5000ms (unless strong objection). we’ll revisit after first full suite run.

Samir Qureshi: +1 with 5s.

Rina Kobayashi: +1.

Julian Moore: +1.

Grace Kim: +1.

Hiro Tanaka: +1. please @ me on PR if kernel stats instrumentation touches runtime hot path.

Sofia Ivanova: cool. Marcus pls write up in the heuristics doc + open PR. Rina/Omar please rerun the streaming mix with fairness window once it lands.

Marcus Reed: ack. will post PR link here when up.

Omar El-Sayed: i’ll add a small bench output section in the design doc with these snippets + a TODO for “phase-aware scheduling”.

Sofia Ivanova: :thumbsup:
